summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — EXPE +7%, COIN +7%, FICO +7%, EFX +7%, INTU +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (DELL -8%, HPE -6%, P -6%, COHR -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: DELL (-8.16%) — Continued AI-hardware selloff on AI-financing worries, extending the Barclays downgrade (to Hold, enterprise-AI timing concerns) that hit Dell earlier in the week. Super Micro and HPE also fell sharply. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: DELL is a large-cap hardware name that no strategy includes. It was also a sector and downgrade-driven slide that began days earlier, so a momentum or gap filter would have seen a stretched, multi-day move.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear company-specific catalyst found. Likely a sector-wide online-travel rally (possibly oil or macro driven); EXPE follows a ~5.7% gain the day before, to a $293 close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EXPE is a mid-cap consumer-discretionary/online-travel name that no strategy's universe includes. With no news catalyst, the news-reactive logic had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap consumer-discretionary names like EXPE to the momentum universe, gated on two consecutive up days with ≥1.5× average volume. Alternatively, add a travel-sector basket signal that fires when BKNG/ABNB/EXPE all rise ≥3% together.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed COIN-specific news for 2026-10-16 in search. Likely a high-beta crypto-equity rally tracking a Bitcoin rebound or US crypto-regulation (CLARITY Act) headlines, but I couldn't verify that.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: COIN is a mid/large-cap crypto-exchange stock, a high-volatility, BTC-correlated sector the bot doesn't cover. A +6.9% sector-beta move with no earnings or gap signal also gives momentum and news-reactive filters little to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a crypto-beta basket (COIN, MSTR, HOOD, CRCL) as a separate universe with a BTC-momentum gate, e.g. enter when BTC 24h return ≥ +4% and the stock is above its 20-day MA, with a tight position cap for its volatility.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst for 2026-10-16: searches found no same-day news. At 766, FICO is far below its ~1,650 level in January, so this looks like a rebound or sector move (software/credit-score), not a confirmed news event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FICO is a mid/large-cap financial-analytics software name that no strategy lists. With no pre-market news or gap catalyst, a news-reactive bot would have had no trigger either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe rule that admits any US name with market cap above $10B, 20-day average volume above 500k and a close-to-close move of +5% or more. Admit it to momentum-trader's candidate list for the next session, with the existing RSI and gap filters applied.

top_movers.catalyst: No single hard catalyst found. EFX rallied ahead of Q3 earnings on Oct 20, helped by mortgage-product news (Mortgage Score Select, Mortgage Ultimate) and the VantageScore-vs-FICO shift. Sources disagree on the date (Oct 15 vs 16).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EFX is a mid/large-cap credit-bureau (commercial services) name that no strategy lists. With no gap or news trigger, a news-reactive filter would not have fired. The move was a gradual pre-earnings drift.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an S&P 500 sector-leader scan to the momentum universe, e.g. top-decile 5-day relative strength with volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average, and let it enter pre-earnings runs of 2+ days before the earnings gate blocks entries.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a software-sector rebound (Adobe also rose) plus follow-through from the Oct 15 Sequence acquisition news. Sources disagree on the size of the move, so this isn't a confirmed single driver.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. INTU is a large-cap software/fintech name that no strategy lists. The move was a sector or news-driven rebound with no earnings gap, so a gap or volume filter would not have caught it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap software/fintech names such as INTU and ADBE to the momentum strategy's universe. Also add a sector-breadth trigger that admits them when ≥3 peers gain ≥3% on the same day.

top_movers.suggestion: Add HPE and similar AI-infrastructure hardware names (DELL, SMCI, ANET) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-wide-drop flag so one-day selloffs of 5% or more with no stock-specific news can be tested as bounce candidates.
